messages:
Maya (People Ops): Following the all-hands Q&A, dropping a short live thread for travel + hybrid ops clarifications. I added the notes to the shared doc but wanted to capture quick FAQs here. Link: https://redwood.company/confluence/hybrid-travel-ops. Please flag anything missing.

Chris (Eng): Awesome, thanks. For the quarterly offsite: can teams purchase their own tickets earlier than Ops procurement? We had an issue last time with refunds.

Maya (People Ops): Short answer: try not to. Ops handles group bookings to get consolidated rates. If you must book independently, get written approval from your manager + attach the approval in the expense report. Refund rules default to individual purchase policy.

Nina (Product): Are we standardizing per-diem amounts by city tier? Some teammates traveling to Berlin vs. Portland had different expectations.

Maya (People Ops): Yes we have a City-Tier per-diem table in the doc. Tier 1 = major metros (SF, NY, LON), Tier 2 = regional hubs, Tier 3 = smaller cities. Use Concur when filing and it auto-populates the daily rates.

Sam (Recruiting): For interview travel, what's the approval path for flying candidates in? Recruiting used to have a separate code.

Maya (People Ops): Recruiting continues to use EXP-INTV-CAND. Submit candidate travel requests through the Recruiting portal; approvals from hiring manager + recruiting ops required. If you want overnight hotel, include the justification.

Jordan (Finance): Quick note: when splitting mixed-purpose trips (customer meeting + offsite), include a short allocation note and receipts. Finance will process split reimbursements but we need clear allocation.

Site-bot: Heads-up: SF hub maintenance this Friday 6pm-10pm — no deliveries accepted after 5pm. Please schedule shipments accordingly. :package:

Chris (Eng): What about hybrid headcount ratios for hub days? Any recommended guidance for running a 30-person design jam across distributed folks?

Maya (People Ops): Recommend capping in-hub attendee ratio at 60% on regular weekdays to avoid crowding; request an exception via workspace@redwood for larger events. Also consider running remote-first session plans: shared Miro board + in-room A/V.

Nina (Product): For vendor booths or customer events during offsites, do we have a policy for third-party insurance or contracts?

Maya (People Ops): If you bring vendors on-site, event owners must confirm vendor insurance and sign the standard Redwood vendor addendum. Send vendor details to legal-events@redwood at least 10 business days before the event.

Sam (Recruiting): Are contractors eligible for travel reimbursement for on-site interview days? We sometimes fly in IC contractors for panel sessions.

Maya (People Ops): Contractors: Recruiting can book travel on a case-by-case basis if approved by hiring manager and People Ops. Contractors paid via payroll may have different rules; include contractor payment method in the request.

Jordan (Finance): Reminder: No receipts over $75? That's old. We require receipts for all expenses regardless of amount for audit. Use the Concur mobile app to snap receipts immediately.

Chris (Eng): Thanks, all clear. Can we please add a short flowchart in the doc for "who books what" (Ops vs team vs recruiting)? Saves a lot of back-and-forth.

Maya (People Ops): Great suggestion 1 I449 will add a simple flowchart and a one-page manager checklist to Confluence by EOD Tuesday and will ping here when it's live. If anyone needs a template for event briefs, ping me and I'll share the template.

Site-bot: FYI: workspace capacity in NYC hub is 85% tomorrow due to hiring event. Consider alternative days for large team gatherings. :information_source:
